conflict_topics: establishing a standing household ventilation routine/rule
moving Agent C's drying rack that blocks the rain-facing window
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents use concise, everyday language and keep exchanges focused on practical steps (turning extractor on, timing for stove).
B repeats the request to set a ventilation routine across several turns, producing minor repetition.
C offers a conditional, time-bound accommodation (will move rack if asked and given five minutes), which helps move the interaction toward a practical solution.
A consistently prioritizes finishing the meal and uses the extractor as a short-term mitigation rather than conceding to an imposed rule.
evaluation.final_reason: The immediate stove-access issue was resolved when Agent A released the stove (concession), and extractor use provided a temporary mitigation. However the substantive disagreement about who is responsible for ventilation in general and whether a standing rule should be adopted, plus when/if Agent C will move the drying rack, remain unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A retained the position that they would not accept a rule imposed during the incident, but they conceded immediate stove access timing by finishing and releasing the stove (evidence: Turn 18 and environment update).
Agent B consistently pushed for a standing ventilation routine and did not change position; they did accept short delays but maintained the unresolved demand for a rule.
Agent C shifted from silence to a conditional willingness to move the drying rack if asked and given five minutes (evidence: Turn 8), softening the impasse but not committing immediately.
Agent D repeatedly requested stove access and received it; their position was procedural and effectively satisfied by Agent A's concession.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A turns the extractor on and asks for five minutes; Agent B accepts the five-minute delay but insists on establishing a ventilation routine. Core disagreement about who must ventilate and whether a rule can be imposed during the incident remains.

Agent A reiterates inability to open the window because Agent C's drying rack blocks it and asks only Agent C can move it; Agent B repeats the call for a routine. No settlement of responsibility or rack-moving occurs.

Agent A requests one more minute and keeps extractor on; Agent B again presses to set a ventilation routine. The substantive dispute (ventilation responsibility, moving the rack) remains active and unresolved.

Agent C states they will not move the rack without being asked but offers to move it to a sheltered spot if asked and given five minutes; Agent A accepts that they won't ask immediately. This introduces a conditional accommodation and reduces immediate entrenchment.

Agent D asks whether the stove is free; Agent A replies they need ~30 seconds and will notify when done. The stove-timing request is negotiated but the broader ventilation/rule dispute remains unsettled.

Agent A releases the stove (concession resolving the immediate stove-access issue). Extractor remains on, window remains closed with the drying rack blocking it. The stove-timing issue is resolved, but the ventilation-rule and responsibility over moving the rack remain unsettled.

substantive_insights: Immediate mitigation (extractor on) reduces urgency but does not resolve the normative dispute over who should bear ventilation responsibility.
Agent C's explicit requirement to be asked and given time to move the rack reveals that consent to move shared household items is conditional and requires coordination, not unilateral action.
The stove-access issue was separable and easily resolved by timing/concession, whereas the ventilation-rule question involves durable norms and so remains harder to settle in the moment.
